title: How far does two hundred and thirty seven divided by eight go?
description: Two hundred and thirty seven is divided by eight in a long division written on the board. Each leftover is regrouped into ten of the next smaller place, past the point, until nothing remains. Keeko's doubt is that the division stops at twenty nine remainder five.
teaching_notes: One idea: keep regrouping each leftover into ten of the next smaller place until nothing is left. Watch for students who stop at a remainder.

video_script.why: The child has regrouped one leftover One into Tenths but not carried long division three places past the point.
video_script.substitution: Each leftover is regrouped into ten of the next smaller place, and the sharing goes on.
video_script.anchor: Two hundred and thirty seven divided by eight, written as long division
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko stops at twenty nine remainder five, though five Ones can still be regrouped into fifty Tenths and shared.
video_script.payoff_line: Two hundred and thirty seven divided by eight is twenty nine point six two five.

final_answer.spoken: twenty nine point six two five

maths_rules: 2 Hundreds = 20 Tens; 20 + 3 = 23 Tens; 23 / 8 = 2 Tens rem 7 Tens
video_script.design: The long division stays on the board; each leftover is regrouped one place lower until the remainder is zero.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a long division frame with 8 outside and 237 inside, and an empty quotient line

marks.frame: the long division frame appears with eight outside and two hundred and thirty seven inside

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book about long division.
<bookmark mark='frame'/>The division is written with eight outside and two hundred and thirty seven inside.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is two hundred and thirty seven divided by eight?

beats.on_screen: the long division frame stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Places in order: Hundreds, Tens, Ones, Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths; an arrow shows a block breaking into ten of the next smaller place

marks.places: the places are lined up from Hundreds down to Thousandths
marks.break: a leftover breaks into ten of the next smaller place; the word regrouping is written
marks.chain: arrows link Ones to Tenths, Tenths to Hundredths and Hundredths to Thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='places'/>In long division, we share the places one by one, starting from the Hundreds.
<bookmark mark='break'/>A leftover is broken into ten of the next smaller place, which is called regrouping.
<bookmark mark='chain'/>Ones regroup into Tenths, Tenths into Hundredths, and Hundredths into Thousandths.

beats.on_screen: Given: 2 Hundreds + 3 Tens + 7 Ones, divided into 8 equal parts

marks.given: 237 and the eight parts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two Hundreds, three Tens and seven Ones, to be divided into eight equal parts.

beats.on_screen: To find: what each of the 8 equal parts gets

marks.find: the share of one part is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much each of the eight equal parts gets.

beats.on_screen: 2 Hundreds = 20 Tens; 20 + 3 = 23 Tens; 23 Tens ÷ 8 = 2 Tens, 7 Tens remain

marks.s1a: the Hundreds are tried and regrouped into twenty Tens
marks.s1b: twenty Tens join the three Tens to make twenty three Tens
marks.s1c: two Tens go to each part and seven Tens remain

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, share the Hundreds. Two Hundreds cannot be shared by eight, so regroup them into twenty Tens.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Twenty Tens and three Tens make twenty three Tens.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Twenty three Tens divided by eight gives two Tens, and seven Tens remain.

beats.on_screen: 7 Tens = 70 Ones; 70 + 7 = 77 Ones; 77 Ones ÷ 8 = 9 Ones, 5 Ones remain

marks.s2a: the seven Tens regroup into seventy Ones and join the seven Ones
marks.s2b: nine Ones go to each part and five Ones remain

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, regroup the seven Tens into seventy Ones. With seven Ones, that makes seventy seven Ones.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Seventy seven Ones divided by eight gives nine Ones, and five Ones remain.

beats.on_screen: 5 Ones = 50 Tenths; decimal point placed; 50 Tenths ÷ 8 = 6 Tenths, 2 Tenths remain

marks.s3a: the five Ones regroup into fifty Tenths and the decimal point is placed
marks.s3b: six Tenths go to each part and two Tenths remain

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, regroup the five Ones into fifty Tenths, and place the decimal point.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Fifty Tenths divided by eight gives six Tenths, and two Tenths remain.

beats.on_screen: 2 Tenths = 20 Hundredths; 20 Hundredths ÷ 8 = 2 Hundredths, 4 remain; 4 Hundredths = 40 Thousandths; 40 Thousandths ÷ 8 = 5 Thousandths, 0 remain

marks.s4a: the two Tenths regroup into twenty Hundredths and two go to each part
marks.s4b: the four Hundredths regroup into forty Thousandths
marks.s4c: five Thousandths go to each part and nothing remains

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, regroup two Tenths into twenty Hundredths. Twenty Hundredths divided by eight gives two Hundredths, and four remain.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Regroup four Hundredths into forty Thousandths.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>Forty Thousandths divided by eight gives five Thousandths, and nothing remains.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Two hundred and thirty seven divided by eight is twenty nine point six two five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the long division
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 29 rem 5; the five leftover Ones glow and split into fifty Tenths; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the five leftover Ones glow and split into fifty Tenths
marks.right: the division goes on until the remainder is zero

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is twenty nine remainder five, and we are done.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five Ones can still be broken into smaller pieces. Five Ones are fifty Tenths, and fifty Tenths can be shared by eight.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Keep regrouping into the next smaller place until nothing is left.
